DERIVED, not asked. Ruff's SIM114 autofix merged two adjacent elif branches sharing a body into an unparenthesised `A and B or C and D`. Directly contradicts R2b-P0 (0% of effort on rote parsing). Found by running the toolchain on checks.py, not by inspection.

Merging branches that share a body is fine in principle; relying on `and` binding tighter than `or` is not. Never write `A and B or C and D`. Ruff cannot produce the parenthesised form, so SIM114 stays disabled and the rule is enforced by NAR007 instead - which needs source inspection, since the AST does not record parentheses.

DERIVED from a tool conflict, not asked. The imported case matters most, because in a monorepo assertNever lives in a shared internal package and ruff cannot see across modules, so it would ALWAYS fire. `return assertNever(unreachable)` is the only form that works everywhere, keeps caller-before-callee, and preserves mypy exhaustiveness (verified: still reports expected "Never" on a deleted case arm).

choice: disable, but on different grounds than SIM114
note: SIM103 and SIM114 are NOT the same class of problem, contrary to how GAPS.md framed it. SIM114's fix is SAFE, so `ruff check --fix` applies it silently - that is what made it dangerous. SIM103's fix is unsafe-only (verified: `No fixes available (1 hidden fix can be enabled with --unsafe-fixes)`), so the documented command never touches it; it can only fail the gate, never rewrite code. The case for disabling it is therefore about its DEMAND - that the last of a run of parallel guards be spelled differently from its siblings - not about autofix risk. Worth flagging because it would be the first entry in the ignore list justified that way.

options: helper that logs and returns the exception
inline log at every raise site
per-item DEBUG plus aggregate WARNING tally
choice: helper at the raise site, aggregate at the handle site
note: Accepted. Helper and six inline logs emit byte-identical records; the helper costs 13 fewer lines. The volume problem is NOT raise-site logging - at default level all three variants emitted the same 10,023 records / 3.2 MB on a 10,000-bad-line fixture. It is the PER-ITEM handle-site log. Logging the item at DEBUG and a per-file tally at WARNING gave 24 records / 1.2 KB with nothing lost under --verbose. Level rule follows: a per-item failure is DEBUG, the tally is WARNING, because an operator cannot act on one line but can act on '4,812 of 10,000 rejected'.

Accepted. Only the match catches a new member: adding TRACE gives `Missing return statement`, while a mapping and IntEnum both type-check clean and fail at runtime with KeyError. Verified independently. The performance objection was unfounded - mapping is 15% faster per call (119.8 vs 141.7 ns), a function-local dict is 6.4x SLOWER, and end-to-end spread is under run-to-run noise. IntEnum additionally makes json.dumps emit 20 silently where Enum raises TypeError, and str() differs between 3.10 and 3.12. Also settled: R2-10 is an ORDERING rule, not a placement ban - a constant naming an Enum member is legal in ### vocabulary right after that Enum.

condition: nest the remainder in output records, never splat it; a frozen dataclass with a mapping field is unhashable
note: Accepted. Q02's recorded options were 'dict of parsed fields' vs 'frozen dataclass' - the choice was about what HOLDS the record, never about field types, so a mapping-typed field violates nothing. NAR005 first fires at depth 3 and Mapping[str, object] is depth 1. Two traps verified: `{'source': path, **entry.extra}` lets an untrusted log line carrying its own 'source' key forge its provenance in the report, so nesting is required; and frozen=True plus a mapping field raises TypeError on hash(), so set(entries) fails at runtime with no linter warning.

Confirmed: grouped guards give NAR008 at line 89; the helper form gives zero, with byte-identical reports and logs. Converges with R4-02 - the same helper resolves both gaps, so it is a genuine pattern in this style rather than a workaround.

DERIVED from a false failure in the length experiment. `vermin -t=3.10` is an EXACT-MATCH assertion, not a ceiling: a file that only requires 3.7 fails with `Target versions not met: 3.10` and exits 1. The documented verify command would therefore fail any conformant file that happens not to use a 3.10-only feature - t3/narrative.py did exactly that. The trailing hyphen form `-t=3.10-` means 3.10 or lower and exits 0. Fixed in SKILL.md and tooling.md.
